name: Haneda-Airport-Terminal-1-2
tagline: Shinagawa in 37 minutes and Tokyo in 43 minutes. Served by 2 lines.
summary: The station is in Ota City, served by Keikyu Airport Line and Tokyo Monorail. Journey times to the main business districts are 48 minutes to Otemachi, 57 minutes to Shinjuku, 52 minutes to Shibuya and 37 minutes to Shinagawa. The station stands 3.1 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 2.5 m. The land around the station is close to level.

terrain.note: The station sits lower than the ground around it, at 3.1 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 3.1 m to 5.6 m, a difference of 2.5 m. These figures were read from the elevation API of the Geospatial Information Authority of Japan at nine points: the station itself and eight compass directions 400 m out.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, neither the station nor any of the nine points within 400 m of it falls inside the projected inundation area. The projected depth differs block by block within the same station area, so check the ward hazard map for the specific address. Inland flooding from overwhelmed drains has no nationwide map; each ward publishes its own, and that is worth reading as well.
stationNote: 2 lines serve the station: Keikyu Airport Line and Tokyo Monorail. The lines are split between operators (Keikyu runs 1 line and Tokyo Monorail runs 1 line), so when one line stops you can change to a line run by a different company. Scored out of 100 from the number of lines and the spread of operators, transfer convenience here comes to 52.

neighbours.note: 794 m away in a straight line. It reaches Otemachi in about the same time as Haneda-Airport-Terminal-1-2.
1705 m away in a straight line. It reaches Otemachi 5 minutes sooner than Haneda-Airport-Terminal-1-2.
